SRC-336:R002.text: 2. VERIFIED DEFECT — UNAUTHENTICATED GRANT FILE: TICKET: CAMP-1930-001 PRIORITY: P0 SECURITY LOCATOR: tools/saipen_engine/campaign.py::verify_operator_grant ROOT CAUSE A grant file is treated as authentic based on local JSON contents. The verifier reads: project_lineage authorized_scopes expires_at It does not establish that the permission-bearing JSON was issued by the trusted operator broker. There is no verified issuer signature, broker event binding or trust-chain proof in the file-grant branch. A caller can supply a self-authored JSON file containing arbitrary authorized_scopes. REPRODUCED NEGATIVE CONTROL An isolated project contained a newly created JSON file with: grant_id: self-claimed and all known scope strings. The verifier returned: valid: true status: VALID_GRANT Campaign admission then returned: admitted: true status: ADMITTED The file did not originate from a trusted operator authority. This is a fail-open authorization boundary. REQUIRED REPAIR Do not treat local JSON as an operator credential. Reuse the canonical SAIPEN operator-origin/broker verification path. Bind the grant to: - authenticated issuer - original operator event - proof digest - exact project lineage - host/session lineage - authorized operation scope - expiration - revocation or consumption status - relevant resource constraints The proof must be independently verifiable. Reject unsigned or self-asserted grant files. A file may carry a signed credential or refer to a trusted broker record, but cannot manufacture authority from its own fields. Preserve read-only diagnosis for invalid grants. Do not allow a missing grant to be replaced by the current request's text or by a guessed proof path. NEGATIVE TESTS A. Self-authored JSON claiming every scope. B. Correct lineage but untrusted issuer. C. Missing issuer proof. D. Foreign project. E. Expired grant. F. Consumed event. G. Replayed grant for a new campaign. H. Valid file modified after admission. I. Valid proof with insufficient scopes. J. Grant removed between worker generations. All unauthorized cases must refuse protected execution. POSITIVE CONTROL A genuine current broker-issued grant must authorize exactly the operations it carries. Do not mark this ticket complete without proving both sides.

SRC-336:R003.text: 3. VERIFIED DEFECT — BROKEN JOURNAL GRANT RESOLUTION: TICKET: CAMP-1930-002 PRIORITY: P0 LOCATOR: tools/saipen_engine/campaign.py::verify_operator_grant ROOT CAUSE The E-### reference branch calls: Journal.open(...) The actual Journal implementation has no such class method. Its constructor instead takes a project root and operation ID. REPRODUCTION Passing E-100 in an isolated fixture returned: valid: false status: JOURNAL_ERROR with: type object 'Journal' has no attribute 'open' REQUIRED REPAIR Do not merely substitute another method until the authority semantics are verified. Determine whether a journal event is intended to be: - an operation receipt; - an authenticated operator-origin event; - a campaign authority grant. These are different concepts. A normal RUN/DEC journal event must not authorize a campaign merely because it exists. Use the canonical event reader and explicitly prove the event is eligible to carry operator authority. If generic E-### events cannot safely serve as authority, remove this grant-reference mode and return a typed refusal. Preserve compatibility only where authenticated provenance can be proven. ACCEPTANCE An ordinary journal event cannot grant arbitrary execution. A valid authenticated operator event resolves through a supported canonical API. Malformed and missing events fail safely. No misleading JOURNAL_ERROR remains for a valid supported reference.

SRC-336:R004.text: 4. VERIFIED DEFECT — DISPATCH LOCK FAILURE IS IGNORED: TICKET: CAMP-1930-003 PRIORITY: P0 CONCURRENCY LOCATOR: tools/saipen_engine/host_dispatch.py::dispatch_next_turn ROOT CAUSE The function attempts to acquire the dispatch file lock. If acquisition raises an exception, the current implementation sets the lock object to None and continues. It then performs dispatch side effects without exclusive ownership. This defeats the new cross-process idempotency protection. REPRODUCTION In an isolated fixture, the lock acquisition was forced to raise. The supplied host callback was still invoked. The dispatcher reported: ok: true dispatched: true status: HOST_ACCEPTED REQUIRED REPAIR Fail closed when dispatch ownership cannot be established. A failed file lock acquisition is not permission to continue under a thread-local lock alone. Classify: LOCK_BUSY LOCK_UNAVAILABLE LOCK_CORRUPT LOCK_OWNER_UNKNOWN Preserve the pending dispatch request. Do not execute the external host callback without a valid claim. Add cross-process tests, not just threaded tests. NEGATIVE CONTROLS - lock acquisition failure; - stale claimed dispatch; - concurrent dispatch from separate processes; - claim stolen during callback; - process termination after claim; - corrupted dispatch ledger; - inaccessible ledger storage. POSITIVE CONTROL One valid owner executes one host dispatch. A later owner safely reconciles an interrupted operation. Never treat ledger corruption as an empty trustworthy ledger.

SRC-336:R005.text: 5. VERIFIED DEFECT — FALSE HOST ACCEPTANCE: TICKET: CAMP-1930-004 PRIORITY: P0 LOCATOR: tools/saipen_engine/host_dispatch.py::dispatch_next_turn ROOT CAUSE The dispatcher correctly handles explicit negative responses such as: {"ok": false} But arbitrary non-refusal return values are accepted. REPRODUCED Host hook returning None: status: HOST_ACCEPTED ok: true dispatched: true Host hook returning an unrelated dictionary: status: HOST_ACCEPTED ok: true dispatched: true Neither response contains a valid host acceptance receipt. REQUIRED REPAIR Implement an explicit typed acceptance schema. Require: - supported schema version; - positive acceptance status; - campaign identity; - iteration identity; - worker generation; - idempotency key; - accepting host identity; - accepted request identity. Validate the returned values against the original request. Returning normally is not proof of acceptance. An HTTP 2xx response alone is not enough unless the endpoint's authenticated contract explicitly guarantees valid acceptance. A subprocess exit code of zero alone is not sufficient to prove a model turn started. Distinguish: REQUEST_PERSISTED HOST_ACCEPTED TURN_STARTED TURN_COMPLETED HOST_ACCEPTED must not be presented as TURN_STARTED. A structurally invalid acknowledgment must produce: ACCEPTANCE_UNVERIFIED The request remains reconcilable. ACCEPTANCE None and arbitrary dictionaries fail acceptance. A correctly structured matching receipt succeeds. A forged receipt naming another campaign fails. A repeated valid receipt is idempotent. A receipt from an untrusted host fails. Only observed TURN_STARTED can prove actual host execution.

SRC-336:R006.text: 6. VERIFIED DEFECT — WORKER SUCCESS WITHOUT EXECUTION: TICKET: CAMP-1930-005 PRIORITY: P0 AUTONOMY LOCATOR: tools/saipen_engine/campaign.py::_execute_canonical_worker tools/saipen_engine/campaign.py::step tools/saipen_engine/supervisor.py::decide ROOT CAUSE The new default execution implementation calls: supervisor.decide(...) and obtains: saipen continue --json It then invokes the corresponding SAIPEN CLI command when available. This is a continuation-control operation. It is not equivalent to starting an AI engineering executor that implements the active Work. If the CLI file is unavailable, the function returns the supervisor decision without executing any Work. The outer step still reports: WORKER_GENERATION_EXECUTED REPRODUCTION With ACTIVE_WORK in an isolated fixture and no actual executor: step.ok: true event: WORKER_GENERATION_EXECUTED worker_generation: 1 progress.made_progress: false The original Work did not advance. REQUIRED REPAIR Do not rename a planning call into a worker execution event. Separate the steps: ACTION_SELECTED EXECUTOR_RESOLVED EXECUTOR_ADMITTED EXECUTOR_STARTED EXECUTION_RESULT_OBSERVED PROGRESS_VERIFIED Connect a real bounded executor through the supported production runtime. If the executor is unavailable, report: EXECUTOR_UNAVAILABLE Do not increment successful execution metrics. Do not report verified generation completion. A launch attempt may be counted separately. Use the canonical next action from continuation assessment rather than blindly assuming every RUN_WORK means running the same command. Verify the actual resulting source, Work and journal mutations. If a CLI command only returns routing instructions, keep executing the required host action through a real executor. Do not simulate implementation by updating STATE or writing RUN. ACCEPTANCE An ACTIVE_WORK ticket causes actual executor activity. The executor receives the exact Work identity and authority. The executor produces an observable result. A completed task is verified using canonical evidence. A failed launch remains a failed launch. A route-only result is classified as route-only. No false productive progress is recorded.

SRC-336:R007.text: 7. VERIFIED GAP — SAIPAL ANALYSIS IS STILL NOT DRIVEN: TICKET: CAMP-1930-006 PRIORITY: P0 AUTONOMY LOCATOR: tools/saipen_engine/saipal_adapter.py::discover tools/saipen_engine/saipal_adapter.py::start_or_resume tools/saipen_engine/campaign.py::step OBSERVED CODE PATH discover() performs: probe() report() status() It does not call start_or_resume(). start_or_resume() exists and calls the SAIPAL next operation. No production caller connecting it to campaign discovery was found. The campaign calls discover(), not the actual analysis driver. CONSEQUENCE SAIPEN can read SAIPAL findings but does not reliably cause new forensic analysis to happen. A pending SAIPAL queue can be reported as ANALYSIS_PROGRESS without any analysis job being started. REQUIRED REPAIR Connect the existing SAIPAL durable cpall lifecycle. Before invoking it: 1. Validate the enrolled source set. 2. Validate runtime identity. 3. Validate authority. 4. Check the current analysis generation. 5. Check whether analysis is due. 6. Resume existing unfinished analysis first. 7. Start a fresh objective only when appropriate. Advance a bounded analysis slice. Observe real SAIPAL progress. Persist source and analysis watermarks. Collect newly qualified immutable audit artifacts. Classify failures and retry conditions. Do not assume a previous report represents new findings. Do not increment the analysis generation merely because report() returned data. Do not rerun unchanged evidence in a busy loop. OWNERSHIP SAIPEN owns calling and scheduling. SAIPAL owns forensic investigation and classification. If SAIPAL CLI needs a change, create a separate SAIPAL-owned handoff. Do not make cross-project edits under SAIPEN authority. ACCEPTANCE A fresh session evidence generation automatically triggers SAIPAL. SAIPAL actually processes it. A repeat call against unchanged evidence is deduplicated. A real qualified finding reaches SAIPEN through the authorized path. No finding produces honest quiescence. A SAIPAL outage produces a typed blocker/retry, not fake completion.

SRC-336:R008.text: 8. Do not conflate: FORENSIC_ANALYSIS AUDIT_STAGING EXTERNAL_AUDIT_PUBLICATION AUDIT_INGESTION PROTOCOL_REPAIR A campaign grant does not automatically grant all operations. Preserve STAGE_ONLY. Preserve canonical audit allocation. Preserve original artifacts. Negative tests must show forged qualified findings cannot publish. SRC-336:R012.text: 12. PRODUCTION AUTONOMY REQUIREMENTS: TICKET: CAMP-1930-011 PRIORITY: P1 AFTER SECURITY P0 TARGET Make the system run on its own after the last legitimate Work item. REQUIRED PRODUCTION CHAIN ADMITTED CAMPAIGN | v CANONICAL WORK ROUTER | v AUTHORIZED REAL EXECUTOR | v WORK RESULT VERIFICATION | v HOST ITERATION CONTROLLER | v ACTUAL NATIVE NEXT-TURN DISPATCH | v NEXT WORK OR MAINTENANCE | v SAIPAL ANALYSIS WHEN ELIGIBLE | v QUALIFIED AUDIT DELIVERY | v REPAIR AND VERIFICATION | v NEXT ELIGIBILITY CHECK When Work is genuinely exhausted: - Check pending sources. - Check pending audit layers. - Check existing recovery obligations. - Check eligible Future Gates. - Check forensic source generations. - Invoke SAIPAL when eligible. - Check bounded HUNT and Improve. - Enter low-cost quiescence if no work remains. Do not invent tickets to keep the AI occupied. Do not hot-poll an unchanged evidence corpus. Do not automatically broaden an operator grant. Do not silently wake unrelated projects. A campaign may continue across many bounded workers, but each generation must independently prove its authority and ownership. A model's final message is not a campaign terminal event. A budget exhaustion is not a campaign completion event. A provider limit is not a campaign completion event. A clean SAIPAL report is not a campaign completion event. A completed current ticket is not a campaign completion event.

The current source includes campaign step and host dispatch machinery, but the supplied archive does not establish a functioning installed scheduler that repeatedly executes the campaign. Do not assume it exists. REQUIRED 1. Identify the native host that executes model turns. 2. Identify the supported callback that schedules another turn. 3. Validate its native acceptance receipt. 4. Prove that the turn actually started. 5. Prove multiple generations use the same admitted campaign. 6. Reconstruct campaign state after process restart. 7. Revalidate authority after restart. 8. Recover pending dispatch through durable identity. 9. Respect cancellation and budget boundaries. 10. Support event-driven or appropriately scheduled wakeups. A Windows Task Scheduler entry may restart an approved controller. It may not grant authority or directly substitute for an AI executor. SRC-336:R015.text: 15. REAL LIVE ACCEPTANCE: Do not report full acceptance without measured proof of: 1. Genuine operator campaign authority. 2. Real worker execution. 3. Actual host model-turn start. 4. Multiple successive authorized turns. 5. Recovery after a worker crash. 6. Idempotent dispatch after restart. 7. Valid SAIPAL source enrollment. 8. Actual SAIPAL analysis progress. 9. Qualified immutable audit generation. 10. Authorized audit transport. 11. SAIPEN canonical Work admission. 12. Verified defect repair. 13. Maintainer disposition acknowledgment. 14. Automatic next eligibility assessment. 15. Clean event-driven quiescence. 16. Safe cancellation and no subsequent execution. Run a sustained real-time soak after the functional path is green. Record: actual elapsed time active execution time quiescent time actual model turns actual worker starts verified fixes new qualified findings admitted audits closed repair chains recovered interruptions denied unauthorized operations duplicate-dispatch attempts resource consumption A fake scheduler and accelerated clock can test contracts. They cannot establish real-world uptime. A controller that only prints status every few minutes is not a productive autonomous engineering campaign. If the installed host is unavailable, mark live acceptance NOT_RUN. Do not forge runtime evidence.

SRC-336:R016.text: 16. CAMPAIGN STOP AND COMPLETION CONDITIONS: The autonomous campaign may pause at: AUTHORITY_BLOCKED OPERATOR_BLOCKED SAFETY_STOP EXECUTOR_UNAVAILABLE HOST_DISPATCH_UNAVAILABLE EXTERNAL_BLOCKED BUDGET_EXHAUSTED QUIESCENT_WAIT These states are not equivalent to COMPLETE. COMPLETE requires satisfaction of the authenticated objective and its explicitly defined terminal acceptance contract. A clean implementation slice is merely a checkpoint when additional eligible work remains. Do not claim victory after one hour merely because every current ticket was marked DONE. Check the campaign objective before determining the terminal state. Do not bypass safety guards, operator authorization or source qualification to avoid an inconvenient stop.

SRC-336:R017.text: 17. REQUIRED FINAL REPORT: STATUS: IMPLEMENTED / VERIFIED / PARTIAL / BLOCKED CURRENT CAMPAIGN: identity, original goal, valid authority reference SECURITY: grant authenticity and publication controls WORK EXECUTION: real executor, actual launch, canonical result HOST DISPATCH: real native host, accepted request, started turn SAIPAL: sources, analysis generation, qualified findings CLOSED LOOP: source audit, Work, verification, disposition CRASH RECOVERY: dispatch and worker-generation evidence TESTS: separate unit, contract, integration and live results SOAK: actual measured duration and generation count REMAINING BLOCKERS: concrete source and owning project NEXT EXACT ACTION: one executable authorized action or a truthful stop reason ===================================================================== FINAL DIRECTIVE ===================================================================== The previous implementation added useful structure. Preserve working improvements. Do not restart the architecture from zero. Repair the verified remaining defects in the real caller chain. An autonomous campaign requires three things simultaneously: VERIFIED AUTHORITY REAL EXECUTION DURABLE CONTINUATION Missing any one of them means the campaign is not autonomous. The intended SAIPAL feedback loop additionally requires: REAL FORENSIC ANALYSIS AUTHORIZED AUDIT DELIVERY VERIFIED REPAIR CLOSURE No paper substitute is acceptable. Continue authorized implementation through successive bounded generations until an actual campaign boundary is reached. Do not mark production acceptance PASS from mocked tests. Do not claim multi-hour or multi-day operation without real elapsed runtime evidence. Do not ask for routine continuation if the host can legally continue on its own. ===================================================================== END SAIHANDOFF =====================================================================
